title: A malformed attribute test with a long bare value hangs the compile forever
text_rewritten:
We compile selectors that arrive from untrusted callers. An attribute test whose closing bracket is missing and whose value is an unquoted run of roughly a hundred ordinary characters never finishes compiling: one request pins a CPU indefinitely and nothing else on that worker makes progress. Noticeably shorter versions of the same input come back with a syntax error immediately, so the cost is exploding with the length of the value rather than growing with it, and a caller only has to add a few characters to move from fast to never.

Rejecting a malformed selector should cost time proportional to its length, no matter how long the offending value is. Well-formed attribute tests must keep selecting exactly what they select today, including escaped characters in the attribute name and the |= and != operators.

acceptance_hint: A bracket-unterminated attribute test with a long unquoted value raises a selector syntax error promptly however long that value is; well-formed attribute tests are unchanged.
